{{update after|2023|11|23}}

'''Theunis Piersma''' (born 15 June 1958) is a Dutch ornithologist, ecologist, and educator.<ref name=nwo2014/> He is among the most influential ornithologists, particularly in the [[Wader|wader bird]] area, in the world.<ref name=nwo2014/> He specifically looks at [[wader]]s and correlations between flock size and distribution, climate, food, predators, pathogens, and their historical-genetic background.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=https://www.rug.nl/about-ug/latest-news/press-information/scientists-in-focus/piersma?lang=en|title=Piersma, Prof. Theunis|date=n.d.|publisher=University of Groningen|access-date=2021-11-19|language=en}}</ref> [[Dutch public broadcasting system#Regional broadcasters|RTV Drenthe]] referred to him in 2012 as the "first migratory bird professor in the world."<ref name=knight/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rtvdrenthe.nl/nieuws/63606/Universiteit-heeft-eerste-trekvogelprofessor|title=Universiteit heeft eerste trekvogelprofessor|date=2012-05-15|publisher=RTV Drenthe|access-date=2021-11-22}}</ref>

He is currently a professor and chair of the Global Flyway Ecology department at the [[University of Groningen]] and Senior Research Leader at [[Royal Netherlands Institute of Sea Research]] (NIOZ).<ref name=profile>{{cite web|url=https://www.rug.nl/staff/t.piersma/|title=prof. dr. T. (Theunis) Piersma|date=2021-11-15|publisher=University of Groningen|access-date=2021-11-19|language=en}}</ref><ref name=bou/> He is also a [[Wadden Sea|Wadden]] biologist at the [[Royal Netherlands Institute for Sea Research]], where he works on sea conservation.<ref name=bio/>

==Education==
Piersma earned his [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in biology and palaeontology in 1980; his biology [[Master of Science|MSc]] ''cum laude'' in 1984; and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] ''cum laude'' in biology in 1994, all from the [[University of Groningen]].<ref name=bou2>{{cite journal|date=2020-10-10|title=Theunis Piersma|journal=Ibis|volume=163|issue=1|pages=309–311|doi=10.1111/ibi.12883|s2cid=242191560 |language=en|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=spinoza>{{cite web|url=https://www.rug.nl/news/2014/06/0606spinozatp|title=Spinoza Prize winner: 'I embrace the fuzzy nature of ecology'|date=2014-06-06|publisher=University of Groningen|access-date=2021-11-19|language=en}}</ref><ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=https://www.rug.nl/staff/t.piersma/cv|title=prof. dr. T. Piersma|date=n.d.|publisher=University of Groningen|access-date=2021-11-20|language=en}}</ref><ref name=nwo2014/> Piersma led his first research trip to Mauritania in 1980 as a student.<ref name=spinoza/> His PhD advisor was animal ecologist Rudolf H. Drent.<ref name=cv/> Following graduation, he moved to the [[Royal Netherlands Institute of Sea Research|NIOZ]] as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoc]].<ref name=bou2/>

==Career==
===Research===
Among his many contributions to the scientific community are proof that a bird's maximum non-stop flight distance was more than double what it was originally known to be;  examination of the [[phenotype]] and its relation to evolution;<ref name=nwo2014>{{cite web|url=https://www.nwo.nl/en/prof-dr-t-theunis-piersma|title=Prof. dr. T. (Theunis) Piersma|date=2014|publisher=NWO|access-date=2021-11-19|language=en}}</ref> and the discovery that "migratory birds can change the structure of their bodies radically in order to adapt to the diverse conditions they encounter on their journeys."<ref name=knight/> His research on the ecology of the [[Yellow Sea]] was a major influence in China refining environmental policy and increasing conservation efforts.<ref name=bou2/> Nature organizations in the Netherlands ended all mechanical [[Cockle (bivalve)|cockle]] fishing in the [[Wadden Sea]] after his work at NIOZ proved it harmful.<ref name=knight/> This was a particular achievement, as he has criticized the Netherlands for not working harder on conservation efforts.<ref name=bio/>

As of 2020, Piersma has published more than 500 [[Peer review|peer-reviewed]] articles and 14 books.<ref name=bou/> Among his many funding sources, he received 2 [[Dutch Research Council|NWO]] grants to research tools used for bird tracking in 2011, and 2 from ''[[National Geographic]]'' in 2014.<ref name=bio/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.org/find-explorers/theunis-piersma|title=THEUNIS PIERSMA|date=2014|publisher=National Geographic|access-date=2021-11-19|language=en}}</ref>

He is heavily involved in Wader's Study Groups and served as vice-chair of the International Wader Study Group for 15 years.<ref name=bou2/> He has also been the editor-in-chief of ''[[Ardea (journal)|Ardea]]'', a peer-reviewed ornithological journal,<ref name=bou2/> and helped found the Global Flyway Network to track birds nationwide.<ref name=marsh/> At [[University of Groningen]], he was the animal ecology chair for 9 years before moving to the global flyway ecology department and serving as its chair.<ref name=spinoza/><ref name=nwo2014/> He appeared as the subject of ''De wereld is plat'' (''The World is Flat''), a 2007 Dutch documentary about his conservation work.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.filmfestival.nl/en/film/de-wereld-is-plat-door-de-vogelkijker-van-theunis-piersma|title=De wereld is plat - door de vogelkijker van Theunis Piersma|date=n.d.|publisher=Nederlands Film Festival|access-date=2021-11-23}}</ref>

===Work in Friesland===
Piersma helped found start the Station Fryslân 2018, a citizens' ecological organization dedicated to looking after Friesland's environment. In 2012, the initiative established ‘Kening fan ’e Greide’ (King of the Meadow, a reference to the [[godwit]]), which enabled farmers, scientists, and artists to collaborate in an effort to "promote sustainable attitudes to nature and the landscape."<ref name=knight/>

===Outreach===
Piersma is known for his creative teaching style, which he tries to make accessible to everyone.<ref name=bou2/> In 2012, he opened the  [[World Wide Fund for Nature|WWF's]] Dutch Jubilee Conference with a theatre performance illustrating the migration of the [[black-tailed godwit]], with composer Sytze Pruiksma providing accompanying music.<ref name=bio/><ref name=knight/> He has two main performances: ''The Sound and Science of Bird Migration'' and ''Music of Migration'', which he has performed in front of [[Beatrix of the Netherlands|Queen Beatrix of the Netherlands]], at the [[Oerol Festival]], and to the [[Bohai Bay]] community while he was there studying the [[Yellow Sea]].<ref name=bou/><ref name=knight/>

==Personal life==
Piersma was born in [[Hemelum]] in 1958; his native language is [[Frisian languages|Frisian]].<ref name=knight/> He currently lives in [[Gaast]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://lc.nl/friesland/Theunis-Piersma-over-de-landbouw-Het-is-tijd-voor-het-echte-boerenverstand-24979378.html|title=Theunis Piersma over de landbouw: Het is tijd voor 'het echte boerenverstand'|work=Leeuwarder Courant |date=2019-11-02|access-date=2021-11-19|language=nl}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
In 2001, a [[red knot]] subspecies from the [[New Siberian Islands]] was named ''Calidris canutus piersmai'' in his honour.<ref name=bou2/><ref name=cv/>
